body.statement: The observed profiles show material cross-symbol dispersion both in one-observation return scale (cited from price_profile) and in the baseline score scale (per-symbol sample_sd_score and related fact refs), and a single sampled symbol records a zero-return observation. A single motivated but unproven alternative is to retain the baseline lookback and direction and add the allowed realized-volatility normalization over the smallest permitted volatility window, leaving the return-magnitude exclusion unset because close-only jumps cannot justify a jump screen. This normalization divides the trailing return by the trailing daily-return SD, which requires a strictly positive trailing SD, so a trailing window whose returns are all zero would be ineligible rather than divided by a non-positive denominator; the resulting volatility-scaled score is not an annual Sharpe ratio and does not remove systematic risk. Trade-offs are an added parameter that must be justified from cited evidence, a deeper warm-up that forfeits eligible signals at the start of each symbol's window, and a changed score scale that plausibly improves cross-symbol comparability without establishing alpha, superiority or tradability. A future independent evaluation would need forward labels on genuinely held-out data, a point-in-time universe, corporate-action handling and transaction costs before any benefit could be claimed; a coherent retention of the unnormalized baseline remains equally acceptable.

body.rationale: The revision changes only the normalization: lookback and direction stay as assigned, the return-magnitude exclusion stays unset because close-only jumps cannot identify corporate actions, and no applicability exclusion beyond the cited findings is added. The chosen volatility window adds no trailing-observation requirement beyond the return lookback, so warm-up and eligible-signal counts match the baseline in the receipts, and no window was excluded for non-positive volatility. A signal additionally requires a strictly positive trailing volatility, so an all-zero return window would be ineligible rather than divided by a non-positive denominator. Costs and uncertainty: one added parameter that must be justified from cited evidence, a changed score scale whose cross-symbol comparability benefit is hypothesized but not demonstrated, and rendered comparisons that are descriptive only and establish no improvement. No alpha, superiority or removal of systematic risk is claimed. A future independent evaluation would need forward labels on genuinely held-out data, a point-in-time universe, corporate-action handling, transaction costs and bid/ask information before any benefit could be claimed.
